source: md/1_PRD.md FR-09 ('Auto-advance when authorised user marks stage complete', PS A) and the §7 stage table (lines 118-127); PRD line 20 records the prototype's workflow states as the BASELINE SUBSET the PRD stage list extends.
note: The per-route stage list and each stage's state mapping. A StageInstance row is a DERIVED record of where an already-authorised transition left the case: the stage service never moves a case, never gates a transition and never changes baseline_version (DEC-0003, PRD §0 — people decide, the system routes). 'active_states' may only name states that route's own transition config (workflow_routes.json) actually defines; a cross-config test enforces this. 'draft' deliberately owns no stage: a case that has not been submitted is not in any PRD stage.
statuses_note: The only StageInstance statuses. There is no 'blocked', 'failed' or 'overdue' status — pendency and alerts are computed separately (Phase 3.3/3.4), never baked into the stage row.
terminal_states_note: A terminal decision completes only the stages the case actually entered; stages with empty active_states (unreachable in the prototype state machine) or stages the case was never in stay 'pending' — 'approved' must never read as 'Appeal completed'. Mirrors workflow_service.TERMINAL_STATES; a cross-config test enforces it.
unreachable_note: Stages with empty active_states cannot be reached by the prototype state machine (workflow_routes.json defines no state mapping to them; PRD line 20: withdrawal, appeal, reopening etc. are unimplemented until verified). They ship with a label and stay 'pending'. Adding a real state for them is a NEW REGULATORY ROUTE — a human approval gate, not a config tweak.

new_technical.source: PRD §7 stage 'Readiness checks' — 'Starts when: Final submission + TER received'; the route's submit transition lands in 'submitted'.

PRD §7 stage 'Scrutiny / Re-Scrutiny' — 'Starts when: Assigned'; the route's start_scrutiny transition lands in 'scrutiny'. Re-entry (after return/resubmit) reactivates this same row — Re-Scrutiny is not a second stage row.
PRD §7 stage 'Compliance cycle' — 'Starts when: Deficiency issued'; the route's return_for_clarification transition lands in 'returned', which is the prototype's deficiency-out state.
PRD §7 stage 'EVC' — 'Starts when: Scrutiny done and route needs EVC'; both EVC states of this route (visit booked, visit held) belong to the one EVC stage.
